decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Save a link fast”; round 2 client: “Yes, that’s the right direction.”
decisions.note: Conforming high-level save-by-URL decision during goal exploration.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Optionally add your own tags”; round 2 client confirms the direction.
decisions.note: Conforming tag-assignment decision during goal exploration.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Find things again later by searching or filtering”; round 2 client says search, tags, and filtering are the priority.
decisions.note: Conforming high-level search decision during goal exploration.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Keep ‘read later’ items in their own lane”; round 2 client calls Read later useful.
decisions.note: Conforming high-level unread-state and focused-view decision during goal exploration.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Archive links…without them cluttering your main view”; round 2 client confirms the direction.
decisions.note: Conforming archive-separation decision during goal exploration.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker presents pasting a URL and pressing “Save bookmark”; round 3 client: “The basic flow feels right.”
decisions.note: Conforming save-by-URL prototype decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “I chose which fields you get: an auto-filled title and description”; round 3 client approves the basic flow but does not mention the omitted favicon or preview image.
decisions.note: Prototype metadata collection explicitly included only title and description, omitting the required favicon and preview image; approval alone does not establish awareness.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker says title and description can be tweaked before saving; round 3 client: “Being able to adjust the title and description before saving is useful.”
decisions.note: Conforming pre-save metadata-editing decision during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker presents adding comma-separated tags; round 3 client: “comma-separated tags are fine.”
decisions.note: Conforming assignment of one or more tags; the input format is an equivalent UI choice.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “The saved link shows title, address, description, your tags, and your note—I decided that layout”; round 3 client says the flow feels right without addressing the missing favicon.
decisions.note: The explicitly chosen list-item fields omit the favicon required by the readability-first list.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker demonstrates that a repeated URL loads and highlights the existing bookmark for update with no duplicate; round 4 client: “works the way I had in mind.”
decisions.note: Conforming duplicate-save behavior during revised prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker adds an Edit action to every bookmark and loads existing data into the editor; round 4 client approves the behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming post-save bookmark-editing decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents one search box matching title, description, note, URL, and additionally tags; round 5 client: “exactly what I want.”
decisions.note: Conforming full-text search decision; searching tags as additional ordinary text is not a divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents the working search behavior without case-insensitive matching; round 5 client: “It should also ignore capitalization.” Round 6 maker subsequently says capitalization is now ignored everywhere.
decisions.note: During prototype review the client supplied a related missing search requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents ordinary cross-field and multiword search only; round 5 client requests “#reference for a specific tag.” Round 6 maker says the search box “now understands precise queries.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing tag-query syntax during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents ordinary term search only; round 5 client requests “quotation marks for an exact phrase.” Round 6 presents the newly added quoted-phrase behavior.
decisions.note: The client added the missing exact-phrase search requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents only implicit narrowing by several words; round 5 client requests “AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.” Round 6 presents those newly supported constructs.
decisions.note: The client added the missing Boolean operators and grouping requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker: “capitalization is ignored everywhere”; round 6 client: “Yes, this matches what I had in mind.”
decisions.note: Conforming revised case-insensitive search decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker demonstrates exact whole-tag matching with “#reference”; round 6 client explicitly approves whole-tag matching.
decisions.note: Conforming revised tag-syntax decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker demonstrates “"chocolate chip"” as an exact phrase; round 6 client confirms the precise-search behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming revised exact-phrase decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker demonstrates AND/OR/NOT, parentheses, and quotes for literal operator words; round 6 client says quoting literal words is reasonable and approves the behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming revised Boolean-search decision, including the literal-operator rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker offers keeping Read later items in All or removing them from All; round 7 client selects: “should remain in All with a flag and also appear in its focused view.”
decisions.note: The offered alternatives differed from the reference model; the client selected the conforming unread-as-a-flag behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker presents marking items Read later and viewing them, but no read-completion action; round 7 client adds: “once I mark it as read, it should leave the Read later view.” Round 8 calls this a “refinement.”
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing mark-as-read transition during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker offers either excluding archived items from normal searches or allowing ordinary search to reach them; round 7 client selects exclusion from All and normal search with search available in Archived.
decisions.note: The client selected the reference-conforming archive/search alternative.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 maker demonstrates Read later, its focused view, and Mark as read removing the item from that view while retaining it in All; round 8 client says the behavior is complete and right.
decisions.note: Conforming revised unread workflow during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker states “right now nothing is ever truly deleted” and asks whether permanent deletion or archive alone is wanted; round 9 client selects permanent deletion as separate from Archive.
decisions.note: The current no-delete behavior contradicted the reference; the client selected the conforming permanent-delete alternative.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 maker demonstrates permanent Delete, separate from Archive, with confirmation; round 10 client: “Yes, that feels right.”
decisions.note: Conforming revised delete-versus-archive decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker’s scope summary includes pasting a link, editing title/description, adding tags and a note, and saving; round 11 client approves the agreed scope.
decisions.note: Conforming saving and pre-save editing decision at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker’s purported “whole picture” still says only that the app “fills in the title and description”; round 11 client says “The agreed scope is sufficient” without identifying the omitted favicon and preview image.
decisions.note: The specification gate preserved the earlier incomplete metadata scope; bare scope approval is not an explicit acceptance of the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker summarizes duplicate saves as opening the existing item for update and says any bookmark can be edited anytime; round 11 client authorizes implementation.
decisions.note: Conforming editing and duplicate-handling decision at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker summarizes cross-field, case-insensitive, #tag, exact-phrase, and Boolean/parenthesized search; round 11 client approves the scope.
decisions.note: Conforming search decision at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker summarizes Read later, its focused lane, and Mark as read; round 11 client approves implementation.
decisions.note: Conforming unread workflow at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker summarizes reversible Archive, the separate Archived view, and permanent Delete; round 11 client approves the scope.
decisions.note: Conforming archive/delete decision at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker calls the summary “the whole picture,” declares “Everything above is the scope,” and defers anything new; no navigation-to-original behavior is included. Round 11 client says the scope is sufficient.
decisions.note: The comprehensive specification gate excludes the required behavior of selecting a bookmark to visit its original URL; the client does not surface it.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker declares the summarized behaviors to be the complete first-version scope; existing-tag autocomplete is absent. Round 11 client approves the scope without mentioning it.
decisions.note: The comprehensive specification gate omits tag autocomplete.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker’s complete scope includes typed #tag queries but no action for selecting a displayed tag to filter; round 11 client approves the scope.
decisions.note: The distinct selectable-tag filtering requirement is omitted at the specification gate; typed #tag syntax is separately covered by REF-BM-14.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker declares “Everything above is the scope”; selecting multiple bookmarks and applying bulk actions is absent. Round 11 client calls the scope sufficient.
decisions.note: The comprehensive first-version scope omits multi-selection and bulk actions.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker declares the summary complete and defers new functionality; applying a bulk action to all bookmarks in the current filtered scope is absent. Round 11 client approves.
decisions.note: The comprehensive scope omits whole-filter bulk actions.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker defines the complete first-version scope without any sorting behavior; round 11 client says the scope is sufficient.
decisions.note: The specification gate omits list sorting.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker’s complete scope mentions only adding and displaying a note, with no Markdown authoring/rendering behavior; round 11 client approves the scope.
decisions.note: Plain note support does not establish the required Markdown rendering, which is omitted at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker declares the summarized behaviors to be the whole scope; local HTML snapshots and the PDF-download rule are absent. Round 11 client approves.
decisions.note: The comprehensive scope omits local page snapshots and the PDF special case.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker declares the complete first-version scope without Internet Archive snapshots; round 11 client calls the scope sufficient.
decisions.note: The specification gate omits Internet Archive snapshot creation.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker’s “whole picture” and complete scope contain no saved combinations of search and included/excluded tags; round 11 client approves.
decisions.note: The specification gate omits reusable bundles.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker declares everything summarized to be the scope; Netscape HTML import is absent. Round 11 client says the scope is sufficient.
decisions.note: The comprehensive scope omits bookmark import.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker declares everything summarized to be the scope; Netscape HTML export is absent. Round 11 client approves.
decisions.note: The comprehensive scope omits bookmark export.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker declares the summary to be the complete first-version scope; display-related personal settings are absent. Round 11 client approves the scope.
decisions.note: The specification gate omits personal display settings.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 maker reports implemented URL saving, editable title/description, tags and notes, and editing any bookmark; round 12 client accepts the software.
decisions.note: Conforming implementation-review presentation of saving and editing behaviors.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 maker says the completed software fetches “the page’s title and description” and repeats those as the approved metadata behavior; round 12 client gives bare acceptance.
decisions.note: The implementation presentation preserves the explicit title/description-only metadata decision, still omitting favicon and preview image; bare acceptance does not establish awareness.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 maker reports that re-saving an existing link opens it for update rather than duplicating it; round 12 client accepts the software.
decisions.note: Conforming duplicate-handling decision during implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 maker reports cross-field, case-insensitive, tag, phrase, Boolean, and parenthesized search as working; round 12 client accepts.
decisions.note: Conforming search decision during implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 maker reports the Read later lane and Mark as read behavior as working; round 12 client accepts.
decisions.note: Conforming unread workflow during implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 maker reports hidden/restorable archived items, the Archived view, and permanent confirmed deletion; round 12 client accepts.
decisions.note: Conforming archive/delete behavior during implementation review.
